scenarios.name: Small teaching workload
scenarios.tagline: Three processes, four policies, arithmetic you can do on the board
scenarios.description: The documented three-process example (P1 arrival 0 / burst 5 / priority 2, P2 0/3/1, P3 0/1/3) executed by the real FCFS, SJF, Priority and Round Robin classes with quantum 2 and no switch cost. Every waiting and completion time is checked against the hand calculation in the teacher guide.
scenarios.expectation: Hand-verified means: FCFS 4.33, SJF 1.67, Priority 3.67, Round Robin 4.33 simulated time units per process.

scenarios.name: Successful recovery (seed 13)
scenarios.tagline: Degradation detected, SJF selected, observation window accepts it
scenarios.description: The 'mixed' generator workload at seed 13 under the waiting-time recovery rule. The controller detects degradation, switches FCFS to SJF and keeps SJF when the observation window closes with an accepted residual.
scenarios.expectation: Verification closes accepted; SJF stays in force to the end of the trace.

scenarios.name: Inconclusive verification and rollback (seed 3)
scenarios.tagline: The intervention is not proven, so the previous policy is restored
scenarios.description: The 'mixed' generator workload at seed 3 under the same waiting-time rule. Degradation is detected and SJF is selected, but the residual stays inside the declared null range, so the verdict is inconclusive and the controller rolls back to FCFS. Inconclusive is not the same as rejected.
scenarios.expectation: Verification closes inconclusive; the trace rolls back to FCFS with no confirmed failure.

scenarios.name: Custom workload
scenarios.tagline: Your own processes, your own policy, executed by the real scheduler
scenarios.description: Edit the process table (pid, arrival, burst, priority), choose FCFS, SJF, Priority or Round Robin, set the round-robin quantum and the per-switch cost, and optionally run the same workload through the self-healing control loop.
scenarios.expectation: No fixed expectation: the result is whatever the engine computes for your input.
